quarterly_data.signal: CFO Aric McKinnis on Q2 segment margins and cash: Probe Card segment gross margin increased to 54.4%, driven primarily by higher factory utilization, manufacturing spending discipline and improved yields; Systems gross margin increased to 48.5% on higher volumes and favorable mix. Non-GAAP operating expenses were $65.7 million or 25.4% of revenue, versus $62 million or 27.4% in Q1; Q2 operating expenses included $4.9 million of pre-production ramp costs for Farmers Branch. Free cash flow was $52.6 million versus $30.7 million in Q1; total cash and investments rose $42.8 million to $349 million. Q3 outlook: non-GAAP operating expenses of $70 million +/- $2 million, including about $7 million of Farmers Branch pre-production ramp costs, and a non-GAAP effective tax rate of 15%-19%.
quarterly_data.figure: Probe Card GM 54.4%, Systems GM 48.5%; non-GAAP opex $65.7M (25.4%); FCF $52.6M; cash $349M

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Mike Slessor on the probe-card segments: DRAM probe cards delivered the expected sequential growth to set another record, with increased HBM4 demand paired with sustained demand in DDR applications. Foundry & Logic demand increased significantly over Q1, driven primarily by probe cards for data-center CPU applications ('an up-step in CPU demand from one of our historically strong customers'), building on continued strength in networking applications, initial momentum in hyperscaler custom ASICs and steady demand in PC and mobile; FormFactor expects continued Foundry & Logic growth in Q3, 'driven by broad incremental demand across our served application space'. Automotive and industrial exposure is 'pretty spotty and nowhere near as significant a growth driver' as HPC and AI.

CAPACITY IS THE CONSTRAINT. CFO Aric McKinnis: gains in output 'have been primarily achieved through yield and cycle time improvement, even as we see more constraints across the supply chain at current production levels', and FormFactor intends to keep pushing those levers through the end of the year before Farmers Branch starts to ramp in Q4. CEO Mike Slessor: 'things are very capacity-constrained across the industry', so FormFactor wants to be thoughtful about capacity commitments to existing and new customers, and until Farmers Branch comes online capacity is 'going to be a little bit of a governor' on share growth at the new fabless CPU customer; he credited the team with 'quickly resolving internal and external constraints' in a challenging supply environment.

PATH TO THE 2030 TARGET MODEL. CFO Aric McKinnis: the implied revenue run rate of the Q3 outlook is 'starting to get close to something like $1.1 billion', and gross margin has moved from 49% at the May Investor Day to 51% as a normalized level at current revenue and mix - 'We're on track... No significant changes in our expectations.' FormFactor is 'primarily counting on seeing that sort of improvement and accretion from Farmers Branch fully in 2028', because ramps 'come with some measure of inefficiency' expected through next year, which it plans to largely offset through operational effectiveness improvements, confining the ramp to initial capacity to the course of a year. CEO Mike Slessor: GPUs, co-packaged optics and custom ASICs are the segments where FormFactor plans to gain more than half of the increase in its addressable market through 2030; it is engaged with all the hyperscalers on next-generation custom ASIC devices and had hyperscaler ASIC revenue in Q2.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 implied run rate close to $1.1B; normalized GM 51% (49% at Investor Day); Farmers Branch accretion fully in 2028

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Mike Slessor on the CPO outlook, hedged: 'I wouldn't say there's a significant pull-in or change in our view' of CPO adoption timing - 'there's acceleration here in the very short term'. How far full-year CPO revenue goes above $20 million is 'a little tricky to judge right now'; 'all of these new technology programs, they always have acceleration, digestion phases'; the adoption rate depends on 'overall CPO adoption by our customers, also yields test time', and going quarter by quarter through 2027 'is probably a bridge too far at this point'. FormFactor has 'a strong position in insertion one' and is 'partnered with the leaders in this overall ecosystem and serving all of the different customer ecosystems and architectures'.
